text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000104's 99215 excess falls mostly on low-complexity patients, but records are too thin to confirm or rule out upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The billing pattern does not look like a sicker panel. The 99215 share runs above the all-provider share in every complexity stratum, and most of these claims are on patients with 0 or 1 chronic conditions, such as the Z09 follow-ups (C0056935, C0057147) and the J06.9 upper respiratory visit (C0057394). Those visits are hard to square with high-complexity decision-making. On its own, this is a pattern consistent with upcoding. The documentation, however, neither confirms nor refutes it: only 2 documented 99215 claims came back (C0057306, C0057862), both supported at high MDM, and the 2 no-lab notes claiming moderate-or-higher data reviewed are weak signals at most. A reviewer should first request charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims, starting with the Z09, J06.9, R21 and N39.0 visits, to check whether documented MDM or time supports level 5."}
